page.layout: One printed page: running head at top with page number 116 at upper left; one column of verse text with italic headings between stanzas; a small catchword-like fragment "Har-" at the lower right edge (a catchword cut off by the edge of the page). No marginal notes printed in the margins.

main_text.p: Serua licet fuerit, Domini tamen illa cubile Contigit, vxoris nobile nomen habens.
Sed contorta tuam vertit difcordia mentem: Factus & es subito frater & hostis atrox.
Inuisi tibi sunt cuncti, tuque omnibus asper: A te fic in te dedecus omne fluit.
Maternum culpare genus iam define, teque Dedecoris patrem dicere discetui.
main_text.head: Amor numinis caput Sapientiæ.
main_text.p: Ædificare paras? sunt fundamenta locanda. Vis nauem? fiat prima carina tibi.
Intento studio petitur sapientia prima? Primum aditum sternet Numinis vnus amor.
main_text.head: Quercus: Hominum dogmata superba.
main_text.p: Quæ procera coma quercus frondente superbit Assolet immundas pascere glande fues.
At lento per humum reptat quæ palmite vitis, Nectareum mensis fundit onusta merum.
Sic quæ dicta ἀνεμῶν ventoso pectore fumant, Non nisi ventoso corda tumore grauant.
At quæ cœlesti veniunt oracula Delo, Vitali vere munere corda leuant.
main_text.head: Vera & falsa bona.
main_text.p: Impare confpicito geminas mihi pondere lances: Hæc grauis ima petit, tollitur illa leuis.
Hinc bona condiscas cum veris pendere falsa: Sunt leuia illa nimis: si nimis ista grauant.

page.notes: The running head and page number are partly worn; "Har-" at the lower right is a catchword cut by the page edge. The line "Inuisi tibi..." and "Dedecoris patrem dicere discetui" are as best read; some words are faint, e.g. "fuerit" and "fumant" (possibly "fumant"). Greek word "ἀνεμῶν" is a reading of a worn Greek word ("ἀνέμων") and is uncertain.
